# iliad-038 — new renderings (6.232–331)

Rows in the form of the conventions table. Every row here is a choice this part makes that the table does not already fix; where a row departs from the Odyssey's English or from a table row, the last column says why.

| Greek | `l` | `i` | avoided on purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| ἑκατόμβοι’ ἐννεαβοίων (6.236; χρύσεα χαλκείων) | "worth a hundred oxen for worth nine oxen" (gold for bronze) | "armour worth a hundred oxen for armour worth nine" | "a hundred oxen’s value" (avoided at ἑκατόμβοιος, 2.449), "a hecatomb’s worth" (a hecatomb is a sacrifice); ἐννεάβοιος is built the same way as ἑκατόμβοιος |
| ἔτας · ἔτῃσι (6.239, 6.262; ἔτης) | "kinsmen" | "kinsmen" | "clansmen", "comrades", "friends" |
| πόσιας (6.240) · μνηστῇς ἀλόχοισι (6.246) · αἰδοίῃς ἀλόχοισιν (6.250) | "husbands" · "wedded wives" · "revered wives" | same | "bridal wives", "courted wives" · "honoured", "respected" (αἰδοῖος keeps "revered", 3.172) |
| ξεστῇς αἰθούσῃσι (6.243) · τέγεοι θάλαμοι (6.248) | "polished colonnades" · "roofed chambers" | same | "porticoes", "smooth porches" · "vaulted", "covered"; αἴθουσα keeps "portico, colonnade" (3.399), θάλαμος "chamber" |
| γαμβροί (6.249, Priam’s daughters’ husbands) | "sons-in-law" | "sons-in-law" | "brothers-in-law" (the table’s 5.474 row is for Hector’s sisters’ husbands); same as γαμβροῖο "son-in-law" at 6.177 |
| ἠπιόδωρος (6.251) | "gentle-giving" | "gentle in her giving" | "kind", "bountiful", "giver of sweet gifts"; ἤπιος "gentle" + δῶρον "gift", rendered by its parts |
| ἔν τ’ ἄρα οἱ φῦ χειρὶ ἔπος τ’ ἔφατ’ ἔκ τ’ ὀνόμαζε (6.253, she of her son) | "And she clasped him by the hand, and spoke a word, and called him by name:" | "She took his hand, and spoke, calling him by name:" | follows the Odyssey (odyssey-076) with the subject made feminine; "clung to his hand" |
| ἦ μάλα δὴ τείρουσι δυσώνυμοι υἷες Ἀχαιῶν (6.255) | "Truly, very much so, wear down the ill-named sons of the Achaeans" | "Surely the ill-named sons of the Achaeans are wearing us down hard" | "afflict", "harass", "wear out"; δυσώνυμος keeps "ill-named" (19.571); "us" is added in `i` only, because the Greek leaves the object out |
| σὲ δ’ ἐνθάδε θυμὸς ἀνῆκεν (6.256) | "and you here your spirit has sent" | "your heart has urged you here" | "bade", "sent up"; ἐξ ἄκρης πόλιος is taken with the lifting of hands in `i` and left open in `l` (the note says both) |
| ἀπογυιώσῃς (6.265) with μένος and ἀλκή | "unnerve me of my might … my might I forget" | "unnerve me and rob me of my might, and I may forget my might" | "strength" (κράτος / σθένος), "fury" (anger), "prowess"; the table gives "might" to both μένος and ἀλκή and the line has both, so the note says so |
| τὴν δ’ ἠμείβετ’ ἔπειτα μέγας κορυθαίολος Ἕκτωρ (6.263, whole-line reply-formula) | "Her then answered great Hector of the glancing helmet:" | "Then great Hector of the glancing helmet answered her:" | the table’s reply-formula and μέγας κορυθαίολος Ἕκτωρ (3.324), put together unchanged |
| ἀνίπτοισιν (6.266) · ἅζομαι (6.267) | "unwashed" · "I am in awe" | "unwashed" · "I shrink from" | "unclean", "unrinsed" · "I fear", "I revere" (each loses one side of ἅζομαι) |
| εὐχετάασθαι (6.268) · πεπαλαγμένον (6.268) | "to pray" · "spattered" | "to pray" · "spattered with blood and gore" | "to make a vow" · "stained", "smeared"; follows πεπαλαγμένον ἄζῃ "spattered with grime" (22.184) |
| θυέεσσιν (6.270) | "offerings" | "offerings" | "incense", "burnt offerings", "sacrifices" (θύος is things burnt; the note says so, the English does not pick one) |
| πέπλον … χαριέστατος ἠδὲ μέγιστος (6.271) | "most graceful and greatest" | "the most graceful and the greatest" | as shipped in iliad-036 (6.87); "largest" was used for the same μέγιστος of a robe at 6.294 in the Odyssey’s line, and that line is kept as the Odyssey has it |
| Ὀλύμπιος … μέγα … πῆμα (6.282) | "a great woe" | "a great woe" | "bane", "curse", "great plague"; πῆμα keeps "woe" (reserved for it in the table’s ὀϊζύς row) |
| ἀτέρπου ὀϊζύος (6.285) | "joyless distress" | "joyless distress" | "cheerless", "sorrow", "misery" (reserved for δύη); ὀϊζύς keeps "distress" (14.415) |
| παμποίκιλα ἔργα (6.289) | "all-intricate works" | "all-intricate work" | "many-coloured", "embroidered", "variegated"; ποικίλος keeps "intricate" (3.327) |
| ἀνήγαγεν εὐπατέρειαν (6.292) | "led away … daughter of a good father" | "carried off … daughter of a good father" | "led up", "took"; εὐπατέρεια keeps "daughter of a good father" (11.235) |
| Κισσηΐς · Ἑκάβη · Θεανώ · Ἀντήνωρ (6.299, 6.293, 6.298) | "Cisseus’ daughter" · "Hecuba" · "Theano" · "Antenor" | same | "Cisseis", "Hecabe", "Theano of Cisseus" (the patronymic is rendered, not transliterated, as at Ἱππολόχοιο πάϊς); familiar English forms for Hecuba and Antenor |
| ἱπποδάμοιο (Ἀντήνορος, 6.299) | "horse-taming" | "tamer of horses" | follows the table’s ἱππόδαμος / ἱπποδάμοιο (2.23) |
| ὀλολυγῇ (6.301) | "with a cry" | "with a cry" | "with a wail", "a shout", "a shriek" (each picks a tone; the note says it is the women’s ritual cry) |
| ἐρυσίπτολι (6.305, Athena) | "city-guarding" | "guardian of the city" | "protector of the city", "who saves the city", "city-drawer"; ἐρύομαι "protect" + πτόλις "city" |
| ὣς ἔφατ’ εὐχομένη, ἀνένευε δὲ Παλλὰς Ἀθήνη (6.311, whole line) | "So she spoke, praying, and signed a refusal Pallas Athena." | "So she prayed, and Pallas Athena made a sign of refusal." | follows the table’s ὣς ἔφατ’ εὐχόμενος pattern and ἀνανεύω "signed a refusal" (21.129) |
| τέκτονες ἄνδρες (6.315) | "builders" | "builders" | "carpenters", "craftsmen", "master-builders"; they made chamber, house and court, so "builders" |
| ἐριβώλακι (Τροίῃ, 6.315) | "rich-soiled" | "of the rich soil" | follows ἐριβῶλαξ "rich-soiled" (1.155) |
| ἑνδεκάπηχυ (ἔγχος, 6.319) | "eleven-cubit" | "eleven cubits long" | "eleven-cubits", "fifteen feet long" (a cubit’s length is not fixed) |
| πόρκης (6.320) | "ring" | "ring" | "ferrule", "collar", "band"; the sense (a band round the spear-head) is as usually understood |
| τεύχε’ ἕποντα … ἁφόωντα (6.321–322) | "tending" · "handling" | "busy with" · "handling" | "polishing", "examining" (each decides what he is doing); ἕπω "be busy about", ἁφάω "handle" |
| ἀγκύλα τόξ’ (6.322, of one man’s bow) | "the curved bow" | "his curved bow" | "bows"; follows the table’s ἀγκύλα τόξα "the curved bow" for the plural of a single bow (5.209) |
| περικλυτά ἔργα κέλευε (6.324) | "very famous works gave orders" | "gave her attendants orders for their very famous work" | "splendid work", "famous handiwork"; περι- "very" and κλυτός "famous" |
| τὸν δ’ Ἕκτωρ νείκεσσεν ἰδὼν αἰσχροῖς ἐπέεσσι (6.325) | "Him then Hector reviled, seeing him, with shameful words:" | "And Hector, seeing him, reviled him with shameful words:" | iliad-016 (3.38), the same line with ἐπέεσσιν for ἐπέεσσι; reused as shipped |
| δαιμόνι’ οὐ μὲν καλὰ χόλον τόνδ’ ἔνθεο θυμῷ (6.326) | "Strange man, not at all fine is this anger you have put in your heart" | "Strange man, it is not fine, this anger you have put in your heart" | "my good man", "madman", "foolish man" (each picks a sense); δαιμόνιε keeps "Strange man" (10.472) with the note on its force; καλά here "fine", not "fair" |
| λαοὶ … φθινύθουσι · αἰπὺ τεῖχος (6.327) | "are perishing" · "steep wall" | "are dying" · "its steep wall" | "waste away" (kept for φθινύθω φίλον κῆρ, 1.491) · "high wall", "sheer wall"; αἰπύς keeps "steep" (αἰπὺς ὄλεθρος) |
| ἀμφιδέδηε (6.329) | "has blazed around" | "have blazed up around" | "is on fire", "burns round"; δαίω "burn", the perfect "has blazed" |
| ἀλλ’ ἄνα … πυρὸς δηΐοιο θέρηται (6.331) | "But up, lest soon the town with hostile fire be set ablaze." | "But up, or soon the town will be set ablaze with hostile fire." | follows the Odyssey’s ἀλλ’ ἄνα "But up" (odyssey-088); πυρὸς δηΐοιο keeps "hostile fire" (2.415); "scorched", "warmed" for θέρομαι |

Departures: none from the Odyssey that the validator would flag. The one unit whose Greek matches a published Odyssey unit (6.295b, ἔκειτο δὲ νείατος ἄλλων) takes that unit’s English exactly; 6.294 and 6.253 are reused inside longer units. 6.274–276 repeat iliad-036 and take its English exactly.
